text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Parliament's constitutional committee astonished by President Martti Ahtisaari's rejection of limiting the president's powers.
- Estonian criminal group has threatened to kidnap two Finns if Finland does not release an Estonian drug dealer from jail in two weeks.
- Parliament's defence committee voted to close the army brigades in Vaasa and in Oulu.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Finnish telecoms group Nokia made a bigger first quarter profit in absolute terms than its bigger Swedish rival Ericsson.
- Pori Jazz managing director Harri Kainulainen to become head of mutual insurer Lahivakuutus at the end of this year.
- Advertising agency Taivas advising Aamulehti-yhtyma on a new name for the media enterprise formed through its merger with commercial television MTV Oy.
- State cooperative leasing company VVO to be transformed to a limited company, says CEO Ben Grass.
AAMULEHTI
- A committee is reviewing a new reference rate for loans granted by the state, the bulk of which are housing loans. The total stock is some 65 billion markka.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Jukka Harmala, chairman of Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners MTK wants a clear regional policy programme to 2005 as a condition to accepting EMU membership.
- The current model for income tax is old-fashioned, says Esko Aho, opposition leader and chairman of the Centre Party.
- The government will respond to an interpellation by the Centre Party on regional policy next Tuesday, and a vote of confidence will follow.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Environmental protection, the Nature 2000-programme and preservation areas terrorise agriculture, says Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners MTK.
- Drugs have become easier to buy and cheaper in Finland that ever before, narcotics police says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292, news@reuters.fi
